text:
Ilya Protas is the younger brother of Capitals forward Aliaksei Protas, and the two have shared a podcast mic, but he's earning his own spot. The 75th pick in 2024 had 124 points in 61 OHL games for Windsor last season, which by our league translation works out to about 49 over an NHL season. Now 20, he has two goals and seven points in 19 games for Washington, playing 11:25 a night.

Our numbers like what happens around him in small minutes. The Capitals get 52.7% of the five-on-five shot attempts and 54.6% of the expected goals with him on the ice, both better than when he sits. His own chances (0.70 expected goals per 60) are decent for a depth forward, and his scoring rate is close to the middle of our talent range. NHL Edge has his speed and shot below average for now, so this is a positioning and hands game. He scored on the power play against New Jersey on Saturday, and Tuesday in Tampa he played 17:18, his most in the last 10 games. If that sticks, he becomes a different player.
